open_points.subject: staff assignment storage uniqueness
open_points.question: Must the staff-access schema permit multiple assignment records for one `(staff_id, project_id)` when at most one is active, as `assign_staff_project` and INV-009 require, or must the operation refuse every later record for the pair?
options: Make only active assignments unique per pair, preserving revoked history and allowing reassignment.
Keep the whole pair unique, which prevents reassignment after revocation and violates INV-009.
open_points.default_guess: Make only active assignments unique per pair; leave the exact storage mechanism to the later persistence contract/code layer.

witness.initial: One revoked StaffProjectAssignment exists for staff S and project P; no active assignment exists for the pair.
events: An administrator calls staff_identity.assign_staff_project for S and P.
The operation attempts to store the required new active assignment.
outcomes: The changed operation and A3 INV-009 create and return a new active assignment while the revoked assignment remains.
create_staff_access_schema's pair-wide uniqueness rejects the insert as PersistenceError, so no new assignment is returned.
witness.observer: The administrator calling the API sees success versus HTTP 500, and the next project authorization check sees access versus no access.

open_points.subject: viewer grant storage uniqueness
open_points.question: Must the viewer-access schema permit multiple grant records for one `(viewer_id, project_id)` when at most one is active, as `grant_viewer_project` and INV-009 require, or must the operation refuse every later record for the pair?
options: Make only active viewer grants unique per pair, preserving revoked history and allowing access to be granted again.
Keep the whole pair unique, which prevents a new grant after revocation and violates INV-009.
open_points.default_guess: Make only active viewer grants unique per pair; leave the exact storage mechanism to the later persistence contract/code layer.

witness.initial: One revoked ProjectViewerGrant exists for viewer V and project P; no active grant exists for the pair.
events: An administrator calls viewer_access.grant_viewer_project for V and P.
The operation attempts to store the required new active grant.
outcomes: The changed operation and A3 INV-009 create and return a new active grant while the revoked grant remains.
create_client_access_schema's pair-wide uniqueness rejects the insert as PersistenceError, so no new grant is returned.
witness.observer: The administrator sees success versus HTTP 500, and the viewer sees project access restored versus still unavailable.

open_points.subject: producer grant storage uniqueness
open_points.text: (`service_principal_id`, `project_id`) of a grant and (`service_principal_id`, `key_version`) of a credential are unique.
open_points.question: Must the producer-identity schema permit multiple grant records for one `(service_principal_id, project_id)` when at most one is active, as `grant_producer_project` and INV-009 require, or must the operation refuse every later record for the pair?
options: Apply pair uniqueness only to active producer grants while retaining pair-wide credential key-version uniqueness.
Keep producer-grant pair uniqueness across active and revoked records, which prevents granting the project again and violates INV-009.
open_points.default_guess: Apply uniqueness only to active producer grants, without changing credential key-version uniqueness; leave the exact storage mechanism to the later persistence contract/code layer.

witness.initial: One revoked ProducerProjectGrant exists for service principal S and project P; no active grant exists for the pair.
events: An administrator calls service_identity.grant_producer_project for S and P.
The operation attempts to store the required new active grant.
outcomes: The changed operation and A3 INV-009 create and return a new active grant while the revoked grant remains.
create_producer_identity_schema's pair-wide uniqueness rejects the insert as PersistenceError, so no new grant is returned.
witness.observer: The administrator sees success versus HTTP 500, and a granted-projects producer subsequently receives project scope versus scoped not-found.
